title: INDUSTRIAL SCALE: 200,000 SQUARE METRES
subtitle: Measure route search, localization recovery, and throughput on a large world.
briefing: The world is large enough that route search and map windows must scale with the authored geometry.
Unknown cells remain unknown until the robot receives measurements; a fixed local window is not a shortcut.
Use Turbo for throughput measurements, then inspect the same evidence at 1x.

prediction.question: What must remain invariant when playback is accelerated?

choices.label: Physics, observations, commands, and verdict stay deterministic
choices.explanation: Playback changes wall-clock pacing only; the plant and ROBOT clocks remain simulation-time based.

choices.label: A faster host changes which route is reachable
choices.explanation: Wall-clock timing is a diagnostic and pacing concern, not a decision input.

choices.label: The viewer supplies far-away goal truth to planning
choices.explanation: The robot receives task intent and measurements, never SIM truth.

running_prompt: Compare 1x and Turbo only after the mission evidence is complete; use Engineering view for work budgets and tick p99.

lessons: Large maps need bounded, deterministic work rather than a magic cell cap.
ROBOT localization and planning remain independent of the renderer and wall-clock pacing.
The performance report is SIM-side evidence and never feeds the controller.
